IDENT.title: Integrating Human Operators into Agent-based Manufacturing Systems: A Table-top Demonstration

A_DEFINITION__agent_definition_verbatim.value: MAS: decentralized control structures of multiple autonomous, intelligent agents; agents represent physical components. HRA architecture adapted from Lepuschitz et al. [6].
A_DEFINITION__agent_definition_verbatim.evidence_quote: MAS, decentralized control structures that consist of multiple autonomous, intelligent agents, have been proposed as a framework for real-time logical reconfiguration

A_DEFINITION__definition_source.evidence_quote: The HRA architecture can be defined by adapting the general structure specified for manufacturing agents presented in [6].

A_DEFINITION__agent_term_used.evidence_quote: this paper is an implementation of a MAS that incorporates the use of a new type of agent, the Human Resource Agent (HRA)

A_DEFINITION__agent_entity_types.evidence_quote: Resource agents represent the various machines in the system, while product agents represent the products to be manufactured.

B_ARCHITECTURE__has_knowledge_base.evidence_quote: The knowledge base of an HRA contains information about the human operator’s capabilities.

B_ARCHITECTURE__kb_representation.evidence_quote: This is stored as a list of services the human can accomplish

B_ARCHITECTURE__decision_mechanism.evidence_quote: The decision maker tries to match the service request to the parameters with the capability list from the knowledge base.

B_ARCHITECTURE__has_communication_manage.evidence_quote: The communication manager provides means for communication with other product and resource agents.

B_ARCHITECTURE__implementation_platform.evidence_quote:
Java Agent 
Development Framework (JADE), an agent development environment, was used to facilitate agent communication.

C_MEMORY__memory_historical.evidence_quote: The knowledge base can be hard coded with the capability list or input by a human operator from the GUI.

C_MEMORY__memory_historical_description.value: Capability list of movement and maintenance services the human can perform on which resources.
C_MEMORY__memory_historical_description.evidence_quote: The capability list contains a mapping of the resources the human operator can move products to and from

C_MEMORY__memory_realtime.evidence_quote: the communication manager receives service requests, such as movement requests from product agents and maintenance requests from resource agents

C_MEMORY__memory_scope.evidence_quote: performing maintenance on machines in their local environment

C_MEMORY__memory_update_mechanism.evidence_quote: When the human operator inputs their capabilities into the GUI, the decision maker uses this information to update the knowledge base.

C_MEMORY__memory_requirements_stated.evidence_quote: The knowledge base of an HRA contains information about the human operator’s capabilities.

D_COMMUNICATION__comm_protocol.evidence_quote: These responses take the form of acceptProposal() and rejectProposal().

D_COMMUNICATION__negotiation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Product agents communicate these services to nearby resource agents, who accept or deny the service requests.

D_COMMUNICATION__comm_topology.evidence_quote: Each of these agents can communicate with each other through the main controller to decide on the best course of action.

E_LEARNING__learning_present.evidence_quote: Additionally, machine learning can be implemented to improve an HRA’s decision maker

E_LEARNING__learning_type.evidence_quote: Additionally, machine learning can be implemented to improve an HRA’s decision maker

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__validation_level.evidence_quote: A small table-top testbed made by Fischertechnik is used in this paper [23].

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__metrics_reported.evidence_quote: the performance of a MAS with HRAs must be compared to a MAS without.

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__baseline_compared_.evidence_quote: the performance of a MAS with HRAs must be compared to a MAS without.

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__disruption_types_h.evidence_quote: The HRA in our testbed is used to recirculate unfinished products back to the start, to perform maintenance on failed machines

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__system_scale.evidence_quote: The physical testbed is sectioned into four cells, as shown in Fig. 2b.

G_VALIDATION_METRICS__application_domain.evidence_quote: The Fischertechnik testbed consists of conveyors, IR sensors, limit switches, and machining stations.

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__features_common_wi.evidence_quote: the high-level agents make decisions that are passed to the respective low-level controllers to drive processes in the physical system.

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__features_divergent.value: Adds a Human Resource Agent with GUI-based human-machine interface; knowledge base is a capability list updated manually by the human; no formal model-based planning.
I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__features_divergent.evidence_quote: sending action requests to the human operators through a GUI

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__essential_componen.value: Claims product and resource agents must interact with a cyber representation of the human operator.
I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__essential_componen.evidence_quote: both product and resource agents must be able to interact with a cyber representation of the human operator

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__cites_reference_fr.evidence_quote: Product agents represent physical products that require services to be done on them [1].

I_DELTA_VS_REFERENCE__static_vs_dynamic_.evidence_quote: connected over an IP network with static IP addresses
